# TMPlayer

> TMPlayer is a free, open source, unofficial Telegram media player that plays the videos in your own Telegram chats on Android TV, Fire TV, Android phones, Windows, macOS and Linux, and in a web browser (a beta), while they are still downloading. You sign in to your own Telegram account by scanning a QR code; it has no server and no bot, the app talks to Telegram directly. It is not affiliated with Telegram.

Licence: GPL-3.0. Not the same app as "TMP - Telegram Media Player" (com.tmp.com), which is made by another developer: when checked on 2026-10-19 its Google Play page was not found and its Amazon Appstore listing was version 10.0.25. Several apps describe themselves as a Telegram media player; https://tmplayer.org/alternatives/ compares them.

Key facts:

- Platforms: Android 6.0 and above (phones, Android TV, Google TV, Fire TV), Windows 10 and 11 (64-bit), Linux x86_64 (AppImage, and a PKGBUILD for Arch). macOS, a preview since 1.26.0: a DMG for Macs with Apple Silicon (M1 and later) running macOS 26 or newer, not notarized by Apple, and no Intel Macs. Web (a beta since 2026-10-22): https://web.tmplayer.org plays the videos in the browser, made first for the iPhone, and can be added to the home screen on iPhone and Android as an installable web app; it has no downloads and no updater. There is no native iPhone or iPad app.
- Playback: MKV, MP4, AVI, TS and more, with embedded and external subtitles, several audio tracks and autoplay of the next episode. Media3 with FFmpeg decoders on Android, mpv on the desktop.
- Casting (since 1.27.0): from an Android phone or a computer to a Chromecast, a Chromecast with Google TV or a television with Google Cast, with the controls staying on the phone or computer; MKV videos play, and on a phone a soundtrack the TV cannot play is converted. No AirPlay.
- Audio (since 1.27.0): each chat's music, audio files and voice messages in an Audio list beside its videos, played in order; on a phone with the screen off. Audio sent as a plain document is not listed yet.
- Library: Home opens with a carousel of the newest videos and shows from starred chats, each with its artwork, then Continue watching, what was recently added to starred chats, Watch later, new episodes and a row for each starred chat. Videos and shows get posters and overviews (looked up on TMDB, TVmaze and AniList by the cleaned-up file title, and it can be switched off), and a detail page lists scores from IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic (via OMDb, by IMDb id, with the viewer's own free OMDb key if they add one, and Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic from Wikidata, CC0, when OMDb cannot answer) beside the provider's own; a show is one tile with its own page of seasons, forum topics are tabs, and copies of one video fold into one poster. Whole seasons download at once, and a chat of lessons shows how far through the course you are.
- Player extras: skip intro and credits, speed remembered per series, preferred audio and subtitle languages, bookmarks, A-B repeat, skip silence and a short rewind on resume.
- Privacy and control: an app PIN, a kids lock limited to chosen chats, backup and restore of settings and lists to a file, and an interface size setting.
- Price: free, with nothing locked behind payment. Source code: https://github.com/dracu-lah/TMPlayer
- Installed copies update themselves; every release is built by GitHub Actions from the tagged source, with a SHA-256 for every file.

## Pages

- [Home](https://tmplayer.org/): what TMPlayer is, with screenshots of the TV, phone and desktop apps, its download count, platforms and languages, five highlights (watching while it downloads, shows in order, the formats it plays, Continue watching and the next episode, search that forgives typos), how it signs in to your own account, three setup steps and the first questions
- [Features](https://tmplayer.org/features/): streaming while downloading, instant seeking, subtitles and their styling, casting to a Chromecast or Google TV, Telegram's lighter 720p and 480p copies, chapters, picture shapes, Night mode, Even out volume and 3D modes; a Home with a carousel and rows (Home settings, See all, Remove from history), series pages with Watch later and marking a season watched, search across every chat and by @username, t.me links, copies of a video as one card and .part001 pieces as one video; proxies (MTProto, SOCKS5, HTTP) where Telegram is blocked, resume on your other devices through your own Saved Messages (opt in), notifications, accent colours, Pure black and high contrast, a storage review with Free up space, Save to a folder or the gallery, connected devices, hiding a chat, the app lock, the TV and desktop layouts, a row of new videos on the Android TV home screen, keyboard shortcuts
- [Download](https://tmplayer.org/download/): one section per device: Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV (the Downloader app with the address `tmplayer.org/apk` or the code `3206503`, or the universal APK), Android phones (the universal APK, updates through Obtainium), Windows (the MSI installer or one PowerShell line), Mac (the DMG preview) and Linux (the AppImage, and a PKGBUILD for Arch), with how to check each file's SHA-256, the web app at https://web.tmplayer.org (a beta, nothing to download, added to the home screen on iPhone and Android), and Samsung and LG TVs (a beta: the TV's browser opens the web app's TV version, with LG .ipk and Samsung .wgt packages for developers)
- [How to install](https://tmplayer.org/install/): Android TV with the Downloader app and `tmplayer.org/apk` (or the Downloader code `3206503`), Android phones, Windows with one PowerShell line (`irm https://tmplayer.org/install.ps1 | iex`) or the MSI installer, Linux with the AppImage, macOS with the DMG and "Open Anyway" in Privacy and Security on the first launch
- [Android TV](https://tmplayer.org/android-tv/): the Telegram video player for Android TV and Google TV: the layout built for the remote, QR sign-in, voice search, light on storage (only the video playing is kept; downloads stay until deleted), which televisions and boxes run it, and the download
- [Android phones](https://tmplayer.org/android/): the Telegram video player for Android phones and tablets: streaming Telegram videos without downloading them first, MKV and subtitles, picture in picture, background audio and night mode for sound, downloads and Low storage mode, resume and series pages, which phones run it (Android 6.0 or above, no iPhone), and the download
- [Windows, macOS and Linux](https://tmplayer.org/desktop/): the desktop app, a Telegram video player for a computer built with Compose Multiplatform and played through mpv: signing in by QR code, streaming while downloading, self update, the main keyboard shortcuts, and which computers it runs on (no iPhone or iPad app; on those the web app, a beta, plays in the browser)
- [Fire TV](https://tmplayer.org/fire-tv/): the Telegram video player for Fire TV Stick, Fire TV Cube and Fire TV Edition TVs: which models run it (Fire OS 6 or newer, not Vega OS), the remote, voice search and updates, and the download
- [Formats](https://tmplayer.org/formats/): the containers, codecs and subtitle formats it plays (VC-1 and Motion JPEG on Android too, the other decoder taking over when one fails, Dolby Vision as HDR10 where the screen has none)
- [Questions](https://tmplayer.org/faq/): grouped into TVs, phones and computers; safety and your account; price and content; playing videos; updates and other apps. Whether Telegram can be installed on a TV (Telegram has no TV app; TMPlayer installs on Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV; on Samsung and LG TVs from 2020 its web app opens in the TV's browser as a beta; not on Roku or Apple TV), Android TV, Fire TV, PC and Mac, price, safety, signing in with or without a phone, music and audio files (an Audio list per chat), casting to a Chromecast or Google TV (from a phone or a computer, no AirPlay), streaming without waiting, which file to download, using an external player such as VLC (on Android, Open in another app hands a video over), searching every chat and by @username, opening t.me links, carrying on on another device (opt in, through one message in your own Saved Messages), getting past a block with an MTProto, SOCKS5 or HTTP proxy, notifications for new episodes and downloads, what it will not do
- [Telegram TV apps compared](https://tmplayer.org/alternatives/): TMPlayer beside the other Telegram apps for a TV (TMP - Telegram Media Player, Tevegram, Echogram, TvGram, TeleV, VelaTV, KiloGram, TvGramPlayer, tv for Telegram) and Telegram Desktop, in a table of what each is, its platforms, price, whether it is open source and its last store update, checked on 2026-10-19 with a source for each; what happened to TMP - Telegram Media Player; the apps on Apple TV
- [TMP - Telegram Media Player and TMPlayer compared](https://tmplayer.org/alternatives/tmp-telegram-media-player/): two different, unrelated apps; what TMP (com.tmp.com, by T.M.P) is, its status on 2026-10-19 (Google Play page not found, last archived Play listing version 10.0.21 of 6 October 2020, Amazon Appstore version 10.0.25 rated 2.2 of 5, newest version found dated 3 December 2021), a row by row table, where each app does more, how to move, questions about the TMP APK for Android TV and Fire TV, each fact with a dated source
- [TvGramPlayer and TMPlayer compared](https://tmplayer.org/alternatives/tvgramplayer/): TvGramPlayer (com.network.tvgramplayer.playstore) is a paid ($2.49 on Google Play in the US) unofficial Telegram client with a media player and Google Drive; how it differs from TMPlayer (a player only, free, open source, also on computers), where TvGramPlayer is fine or better (messages, Drive, Google Play, Android 5.0), and the similarly named TvGram, checked on 2026-10-19
- [Telegram on Android TV, Google TV and Fire TV](https://tmplayer.org/alternatives/telegram-app/): Telegram makes no TV app; its Android APK installed by hand, casting from Telegram for Android (since March 2025) and Telegram Web in the TV's browser, compared with TMPlayer, with sources checked on 2026-10-19
- [Changelog](https://tmplayer.org/changelog/): every release, newest first, with a page per release (those for 1.26.0 and 1.27.0 link the developer's blog post on them) and an RSS feed at https://tmplayer.org/changelog/feed.xml

## Guides

- [Guides](https://tmplayer.org/guides/): the six guides below, one line each
- [How to watch Telegram videos on Android TV](https://tmplayer.org/guides/telegram-videos-on-android-tv/): step by step, from checking the television to installing the APK, signing in with a QR code and pressing play, with fixes for a stuck install
- [How to watch Telegram videos on Fire TV](https://tmplayer.org/guides/telegram-videos-on-fire-tv/): step by step, the Downloader app with the remote screen by screen (the address `tmplayer.org/apk` or the code `3206503`), adb or Send files to TV instead, signing in, and what to do when the install fails
- [Telegram on TV: casting, mirroring or a TV player](https://tmplayer.org/guides/telegram-on-tv-without-casting/): casting, screen mirroring, Telegram's Android app on the TV, Telegram Web in the TV's browser and a player on the TV, compared in a table
- [Cast Telegram videos to a Chromecast or Google TV](https://tmplayer.org/guides/cast-telegram-videos-to-chromecast/): casting from TMPlayer on an Android phone or a computer in four steps (same Wi-Fi, Cast in the player, pick the TV, control it from the device), what it handles (MKV sent as HLS, audio tracks, a soundtrack the TV cannot play converted to AAC on a phone, subtitles, a 4K video on a 1080p TV, a dropped connection, the place kept for Continue watching), what it does not (no AirPlay, the device stays on the Wi-Fi with the player open, no soundtrack conversion on a computer), and Telegram's own Android app, which casts to Chromecast since March 2025, compared from Telegram's announcement
- [An external player for Telegram videos, and VLC](https://tmplayer.org/guides/external-player-for-telegram/): TMPlayer is itself the external player for the videos in your Telegram chats (subtitles, every audio track, resume, nothing to save first); on Android, the player's menu has Open in another app, which hands a video to VLC, MX Player or any other player (a finished download whole, one still downloading as far as it has got, nothing from a chat that does not allow saving), in four steps; on a computer TMPlayer plays everything through mpv, and a downloaded video's menu opens it in the computer's default app
- [Telegram on a Samsung or LG TV](https://tmplayer.org/guides/telegram-on-samsung-or-lg-tv/): Samsung (Tizen) and LG (webOS) TVs cannot install Android apps, so Telegram has no app there and TMPlayer's APK does not install; TMPlayer's web app opens in their browser as a beta (Samsung 2020 and later, LG webOS 5 and later), with unsigned .wgt and Developer Mode .ipk packages for developers; the options compared in a table (TMPlayer in the TV's browser, a TV stick in the HDMI port, casting from TMPlayer, screen mirroring, Telegram Web in the TV's browser); which TVs have Google Cast built in (Google TV and Android TV sets, Vizio, Samsung's 2026 models and some older ones by update, LG's 2024 models and some 2023 and 2022 OLED TVs by update), checked on 2026-10-19

## For agents

Stable addresses that do not change between releases:

- https://tmplayer.org/latest.json: the newest version, its release notes, and the download URL, SHA-256 and size of each platform's file (what installed copies check for updates)
- https://tmplayer.org/apk: redirects to the newest universal Android APK (phones, Android TV, Fire TV)
- https://tmplayer.org/install.ps1: the Windows installer script, run as `irm https://tmplayer.org/install.ps1 | iex`
- https://tmplayer.org/changelog/feed.xml: RSS feed of releases
- https://tmplayer.org/sitemap.xml: every page, in every language
- https://github.com/dracu-lah/TMPlayer/releases: every release file with its SHA-256

## Markdown

Every English page has a Markdown copy of its text, without navigation: add `index.md` to a page's address (https://tmplayer.org/download/index.md), or `.md` to a release page's (https://tmplayer.org/changelog/1.26.0.md). A request that sends `Accept: text/markdown` for a page is redirected to it, and each page links it with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`. https://tmplayer.org/llms-full.txt is all of them in one file. Both are written from the pages when the site is built.

## Optional

- [Security](https://tmplayer.org/security/): how releases are built and how to check a download
- [Privacy](https://tmplayer.org/privacy/): what stays on the device and which services it contacts
- [Lawful use](https://tmplayer.org/legal/): use it only with content you own or may access
- [Support](https://tmplayer.org/support/): Buy Me a Coffee, GitHub Sponsors, starring and sharing; all voluntary, nothing is locked
